By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Techno Tots

The first three years of a babies life are the most important when it comes to brain development, the brain grows 80% in that time. When a child is born the brain is 20% wired up. To “wire up” synaptic connections need to be made, 700 synaptic connections are made in a child’s brain every second for first 3 years.
It is a time of rapid cognitive, linguistic, social, emotional and motor development. These experiences come through having someone to bond with, to talk to, communicate with, all the time.

The child's brain grows as she or he sees, feels, tastes, smells and hears. Each time the child uses one of the senses, a neural connection is made in the child's brain. New experiences repeated many times help make new connections, which shape the way the child thinks, feels, behaves and learns now and in the future.

Ipads were launched in 2010 and in 6 years there are now an estimated 2,5 – 3 million tablets in South African homes and a plethora of apps aimed at very young children. For some parents, it is very easy to give a child a tablet to play on. They are a way to take “time out” for the exhausted parent or they can restore calm after a temper tantrum.
Evidence has shown that there is an addictive quality to tablets.
The earlier children are hooked on screens, the more difficult it is to wean them off.
But what effect is this having on their young minds? How is it shaping their experiences? And how do we as parents deal with the technology. The impact these mobile devices are having on the development and behaviour of children is still relatively unknown.

Child development specialists have been very critical of television for young children, saying that it is a passive but do the same rules apply to tablets which are interactive?

There is a growing body of research that technology can be both beneficial and harmful to different ways in which children think. Frequent exposure to technology is wiring the brain in very different ways that that in the previous generations.

This is the rise of the techno tots, a generation who will put others' claims to be digital natives to shame. Technology has developed so swiftly over the last decade that parents and educators have little information about how being immersed in the digital world will affect children's long-term development.


Neurologist "Mobile devices are everywhere and children are using them more frequently at young ages. The impact these mobile devices are having on the development and behaviour of children is still relatively unknown.


Issues
American Academy of Paediatrics suggests no screen time for kids and under 2 years and no more than 2 hours for older children.
If adults are known to have screen addiction how will it affect younger brains.
Will children learn self regulation/self control?
How does it affect developing brains?
Televsion seen as bad for children as passive, but Ipad time is interactive. Does that change anything?
Experiment when mothers and children played on iPads mothers spoke less to child than when they play with physical toys. How affects vocalization.

Joan Tindale - who runs Greenpark Nursery School. They have no iPads believes children should be stimulated to explore their worlds,
Lots of outside play. Kids don’t need screens . Outspoken about use of iPads.

Nicole Hilburn - mother at Greenpark Nursery School. Runs a physiotherapy practice. Deals a lot with children of low muscle tone. Attended a conference recently in States, America Academy of Paediatrics recommended that kids under 2 should have no screen time, citing concerns about language delays and disrupted sleep. Kids from 2-6 years old should only have 20 - 40 mins a day.The academy’s new report drew on studies showing that TV, whether it’s the parent or the child watching, interferes with “talk time” between parent and child, which is crucial to language development.

Liz Senior - Occupational Therapist founder of Clamber Club. An organisation that encourages kids to explore their world through movement. She would also be able to talk about handwriting and fine motor skills.
(She can organise groups of women with kids who we could do interviews with)

Apple’s iTunes now stocks more than 700 apps for children, including ones that promise to “develop hand-eye coordination and focusing skills in young babies” or teach “fine motor skills” to infants “from 0 to 2.5 years old.”

Little Ashford Pre-School – Jena Mukina and Marli Hoffman
First crèche in SA to offer ipads. How do we prepare our children for their future? World fast paced, vastly different to our own world and technology driven. When do you start preparing your children for this future? Below age of 3 children have twice as many synapses as they will have for the rest of their adult lives. Human brain grows 80% before the age of 3. Technology can not replace anything that you would do traditionally at a school.

Paediatric neurologist – Dr Bham

Visuals of kids and iPads

Press Release:


Techno Tots
Just seven years ago, tablet devices were not available. Today there are over three million in use, with a plethora of apps targeted specifically at young children. While many institutions of learning have already incorporated the tablet as an educational tool - even for children as young as two years old - there is growing concern about the effect of this technology on young brains. Carte Blanche asks: how much is too much screen time?


Script:


TechnoTots Script

Link
This is the rise of the technotots, a generation that will put all others to shame in terms of being digital natives but there is also growing concern about the fast paced technology and it’s long term effects on the brains of little children.

YouTube I want my ipad

V/O
In the same way that tablets and smart phones are seen as digital cocaine for adults. Youngsters can easily become addicted to their shiny screens.


V/O
Child development experts are warning parents that too much screen time can damage their toddler’s development. Apart from their addictive quality, some studies have suggested that it adversely affects speech and language skills.

Joan Tindale head of ParkView Nursey School has been in child education for 40 years, and believes that children learn speech and language from real people – not from apps or tv shows.

Bongani
“What is wrong with screens?”

Joan
“Lots,
Screen time takes away completely from inter personal relationships, so children have lost the skill of conversing, that’s a big one in pre school we see that , that even in last 5 years, you would have children in a group wanting to discuss topic with them and they don’t have general knowledge. The knowledge they have they have got from screens.

Link
When South Africa hosted the world cup in 2010, tablet devices were not available, today there are an estimated 3 million in use and many of them with a plethora of apps targetted specifically at young children.

V/O
Although they have not been around that long there is already a mass of research showing links between excessive screen-time and obesity, low muscle tone, aggression, poor social skills, depression and academic under-achievement.

V/O
Dr Brendan Belsham is a paediatric psychiatrist specialising in ADHD.

“The studies that have been done suggest that kids who are exposed to more than 2 or 3 hours of elecronic screens per day in those first two or three years of life have a higher incidence of attention problems, self regulation problems, impulsivity all of which we know are part and parcel of the adhd syndrome.”


V/O
Nicole Hilburn is a paediatric physiotherapist and is deeply concerned about the impact that screens can have on young developing minds and protects her daughters who are both under 5 years old as much as possible.

Bongani
“Now you as a family have decided that they are not going to have any screen time?

Nicole
“I think it is exactly that it will take away time that they would have spent playing in other concrete ways, doing puzzles engaging in constructive play, the more screen time they are engaging in the less of that kind of play they are doing and there is quite a small window for that type of play and those developmental skills are important in a child’s life.”

V/O
But some parents may equally feel that learning about technology is also an important skill that their children need to master.

V/O
Little Ashford is a pre school that uses tablets as part of their teaching regime believing that this provides their children a competitive edge in a technologically driven world. Jena Mukhina and Marli Hoffman are its directors.

Jena
“65% of pre schoolers will be in jobs that they have never heard of before. So we are trying to make sure that when our preschoolers are so comfortable with technology that when they get to pre primary or primary school its nothing that they have never seen before and they know how to engage with it.”

V/O
The children’s access to tablets is strictly controlled and it has been carefully planned by the educators to enhance the themes that they are learning during the week.

Marli
“Their exposure is also extremely limited. The maximum is 15 minutes a day and that’s for the older children and the younger children get a maximum of 5 minutes a day.”






V/O
Brain development is crucial in a child’s first few years of life, every second 700 to 1,000 new neural connections are formed. These are the connections that build brain architecture – the foundation upon which all later learning, behavior, and health depend.

Brendan
“The first two or three years of a child’s life are characterisd by rapid brain growth such that the brain actually trebles in size in the first two years of life.”

V/O
And it is this phase of growth that Liz Senior believes we should optimise on.
She is an occupational therapist and founder of the Clamber Club an organisation that provides movement and stimulation classes for young ones.

Liz
“If you imagine a child for example looking on a screen at an orange and someone says that is an orange you are getting a visual cue to it and and you are getting an auditory cue but can you imagine what the understanding is when you feel an orange when you taste an orange , smell an orange so it is those real life experiences that I think children miss out on when they are looking at a screen.

V/O
But how much screen time is too much?

Nicole
“The guidelines are that children under the age of 2 years should have no screen time at all and above 2 years it should be a maximum of an hour a day and that is of any screen an ipad. Cell phone and television.”


V/O
But is technology to blame? Isn’t the fault really with the lack of time we as a society spend with our children in meaningful ways?
Some parents use the screens as pacifiers and don’t regulate the time their children spend on them.
We spoke to a couple of parents and asked them how they approach the issue of screen time.


Voxpops

“OK my view on kids under two having having access to digital devices it is not necessarily a bad thing but you need to manage it properly because there are a lot of negative things out there.”

“They almos never watch televsio, they get about 30 minutes a week of TV time.”

“I usually give it to her because she can play around with puzzles and she can see which shape goes where.”

“As a result we find that both our children play with them for a little but then easily get bored and move straight on to their toys.”

Link
Many modern parents simply do not have the time to get involved in every aspect of their child’s upbringing. Giving them a device is the easiest thing especially when that child is having a temper tantrum but what are the long term effects of too much exposure?”

Bongani
“In your practice what harmful effects have you seen on kids who have been over exposed to devices?”

Nicole
What we see in terms of the children that we treat is probably reduced endurance and srength not as much time playing outside and this often has a repercussion in terms of the classroom situation. They don’t have well developed core stability and so they are unable to sit in a classroom listen to whats happeninga nd produce a fine motor output like writing or reading. Often misdiagnosed with concentration difficulties as a result.

V/O
And when children have had too much screen time it is very difficult to wean them off again.

Bongani
“When this type of addiction forms in such a small brain what does it do?”



Brendan
So we are almost spoiling the brain we are changing the threshold point at which that child is going to respond favourably to a given environmental stimulation and that is very worrying, it’s worrying not only for the potential risk of later substance abuse but also in terms of everyday life, school life for example


V/O
Little Ashford stresses that access to screens should be limited and controlled.

Bongani
“So what is the rule of thumb in terms of appropriate exposure?”

Marli
“There always needs to be a learning experience for the child. If they are just getting an ipad and they are not being supervised and shown what to do that’s where the issue comes in but I feel that children are going to be exposed to it everywhere and we need to teach them to be exposed to it in the right way and teach them that balance of playing outside, reading from a normal book but also being able to use an ipad.

Promo 1 - 10 secs

In the first 3 years of life, 700 – 1000 neural connections form every second in a child’s brain, should we as parents be allowing our children so much screen time?

Promo 2 15 secs

Although they have only been with us for 6 years, many experts are warning parents on the dangers of too much screen time.

“Screen time is taking away from the essential development children need.”

How much screen time do you allow your children?

Promo 3 15 secs

Meet the TechnoTots, a generation born into a world of tablets and smart phones, but there is also growing concern about the fast paced technology and it’s long term effects on the brains of little children.
